tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The organisation, the signed-in person, the projects this connection may use, plan usage and limits, and the scopes granted. (Requires scope mcp:read.)

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: The projects this connection may use. (Requires scope mcp:read.)

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project in the organisation. The new project is added to this connection, so the other tools can use it. (Requires scope projects:create.)

tools.name: create_session
tools.description: Create a video session in a project. Returns its id; browsers join it with connection tokens. Subject to the plan’s limits, and fires the session.created webhook. (Requires scope mcp:write.)

tools.name: create_connection_token
tools.description: Mint a short-lived connection token for one participant to join a session from a browser — for trying the integration locally. In production the app’s server mints these with its own key. (Requires scope mcp:write.)

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: Recent sessions in a project, newest first. (Requires scope mcp:read.)

tools.name: get_session_manifest
tools.description: The raw session manifest: every participant and track that actually holds recorded media, with time bounds. A track is listed only once media reached it. (Requires scope mcp:read.)

tools.name: request_transcript
tools.description: Transcribe a session that has ended: speech-to-text over every participant’s microphone, written as timed cues per speaker and language. Idempotent: a transcript already queued, running or up to date is returned. Billed per minute of speech after silence is removed; the Free plan includes 60 minutes

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: A session’s transcript: its status (pending, processing, ready, failed or skipped, with error_code), the languages it holds, and cues with speaker (the participant’s user id), language, text and times in ms from the start of the recording. (Requires scope mcp:read.)

tools.name: verify_session
tools.description: Prove an integration works: read the recording of a session the app published into, and check each expected participant actually carried media on each expected track. findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_server_key" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Mint a restricted server key (rk_live_…) for one project, for the app’s server-side environment. It can only create sessions, mint connection tokens and read ma…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_transcript, get_guide · Private data: create_session, create_connection_token, create_server_key · Public sink: create_session · Destructive: run_media_check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_transcript, get_guide · Private data: create_session, create_connection_token, create_server_key · Public sink: create_session · Destructive: run_media_check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
